summary: Prepare shared native batch counters for repeated FFI calls

delivery.outcome: Prepare reusable batch counters for SDK or installed native donor with one batch FFI per hot call and no repeated artifact audits; preserve old APIs and independently merge verified artifacts.
nonGoals: No algorithm/ABI/schema/runtime dependency/platform or consumer migration, streaming API expansion, hot reload/global deduplication, production speed guarantee, download or registry release/deploy.

architecture.decision: Add prepare_ascii_token_batch_counter returning callable over iterable[bytes], supporting Rust SDK, compiled-python and existing pinned installed Rust-only donor. Extract shared preparation selection from scalar factory, batch symbol binder and normalization/packing/status helpers; preserve count_ascii_tokens_many validation/packing/capability ordering and iterator APIs. Callable retains native function/library, performs no file or metadata lookup per batch. Audit each preparation before cached handle reuse; optional missing batch symbol fails without breaking scalar. Test ownership/drift/ABI/errors/types/empty/generator/lifetime/threads/shared handles. Actual source-donor proof without tools/build deps/exports plus paired warmed scalar-loop vs batch timing on fixed corpus, no performance threshold.
dataChanges: None; installed snapshot/backend and on-wire manifests unchanged.
architecture.rollback: Protected reviewed revert; existing scalar/many/stream factories stay compatible; preserve old dist and all ignored data.

validation.evidence: Prepared batch validation, one FFI call, real buffer lengths, errors/empty/generator/compiled behavior, audit-before-cache/lifetime/symbol/default regressions.

Full suites and actual no-toolchain/build-dep source-donor scalar+batch clients share handle; threaded parity, no hot file reads/export; paired timing/no threshold, final artifacts/reused NL8, indexed canonicalv26/pinned Docs.
Exact-head local/remote gates, independent approval/merge, postmerge smoke, owner release and preserved cleanup.
